newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends weaker on stop-loss selling.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends weaker on stop-loss selling.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended weaker on Wednesday at C$1.3892 (US$0.7198) from this morning's open of C$1.3844 (US$0.7223) under pressure from stop-loss selling, traders said.
* They said investors in North American trading hours reversed a flurry of buying from German investors overnight during European trade.
The Canadian dollar ended weaker on Wednesday at C$1.3892 (US$0.7198) from this morning's open of C$1.3844 (US$0.7223), pressured by stop-loss selling, traders said.
They said investors during North American trading hours reversed a flurry of buying from German investors overnight in European trade.

"I'm a bit disappointed that the Canada didn't do better today," said Stephen Wateridge, managing director of corporate foreign exchange at CIBC-Wood Gundy Inc. "This is the first day in a while that we saw corporate buyers of dollars."

Wateridge said Canada's currency is expected to come under increasing pressure ahead of economic data from the U.S. on Friday. A Reuter survey of economists forecast March producer prices will be reported unchanged on Friday.

Analysts said that if the U.S. producer prices data is higher than expected, renewed speculation about a possible rise in U.S. interest rates will emerge, increasing pressure on the Canadian dollar on the expectation that interest rate spreads will widen.
"It's probably going to be just a little wobbly ahead of those U.S. numbers on Friday," Wateridge said.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar moved up to 1.2418 marks from Tuesday's close of 1.2348 marks and jumped to 91.21 yen from Tuesday's 90.92 yen.
